mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is NOT a correct definition of a unit cell in a crystal lattice?

options.A: The smallest repeating three‑dimensional portion of a crystal that, when stacked together in three dimensions, reproduces the entire lattice.
options.B: A single isolated atom that does not repeat in the crystal.
options.C: The outermost layer of atoms on a crystal surface.
options.D: A defect or vacancy within the crystal lattice.

mcqs.answer: A single isolated atom that does not repeat in the crystal.
mcqs.explanation: A unit cell is the smallest repeating three‑dimensional building block of a crystal that, when translated in space, generates the whole lattice. Options A and C describe aspects of the crystal but not the definition, and D describes a defect, not the basic structural unit. Option B describes an isolated atom, which does not represent the periodic nature of a unit cell, making it the incorrect definition.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify primitive and centred unit cells
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a primitive unit cell from a centred unit cell?

options.A: A primitive unit cell contains lattice points only at its corners, whereas a centred unit cell has additional lattice points inside the cell.
options.B: A primitive unit cell always has more atoms than a centred unit cell.
options.C: A centred unit cell is always larger in volume than a primitive cell of the same lattice type.
options.D: A primitive unit cell always has a coordination number of 12.

mcqs.answer: A primitive unit cell contains lattice points only at its corners, whereas a centred unit cell has additional lattice points inside the cell.
mcqs.explanation: In a primitive cell the only lattice points are at the eight corners; any additional points (body‑centred, face‑centred, etc.) make the cell a centred one. Options B, C and D are false: primitive cells can have fewer atoms, volume depends on the specific lattice, and coordination number is a property of the lattice, not of the cell type.

mcqs.question: Which pair of crystal lattices have the same coordination number?

options.C: Face‑centred cubic and hexagonal close packed
options.D: Simple cubic and hexagonal close packed

mcqs.answer: Face‑centred cubic and hexagonal close packed
mcqs.explanation: Both face‑centred cubic (FCC) and hexagonal close packed (HCP) structures have a coordination number of 12, meaning each atom touches 12 nearest neighbours. Simple cubic has CN = 6 and body‑centred cubic has CN = 8, so the other options are incorrect.

mcqs.question: In metallic solids, which property is most directly affected by whether the crystal adopts a primitive or a centred unit cell?
mcqs.explanation: The type of unit cell determines how efficiently atoms are packed. Centered cells (e.g., body‑centred or face‑centred) have higher packing efficiency than primitive cells, leading to a higher mass per unit volume, i.e., greater density. Melting point and conductivity also depend on bonding but are less directly linked to the primitive vs centred distinction, and color is unrelated.
